common_name: Supertunia Vista Bubblegum Petunia (Extremely Vigorous Spreading Pink Petunia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Supertunia Vista Bubblegum spreads much more vigorously than a typical petunia, easily covering three to four feet, making it better suited to large containers, hanging baskets, and landscape beds than small pots.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, giving it ample room to spread since it is far more vigorous than a standard petunia. Supertunia Vista Bubblegum produces an enormous mounding, trailing plant covered in clear bubblegum-pink flowers from spring through frost, largely self-cleaning so it needs little deadheading to keep flowering heavily. Its exceptional vigor makes it a favorite for large mixed containers, hanging baskets, and mass landscape plantings where a smaller petunia would be overwhelmed by neighboring plants. Regular fertilizing supports its vigorous growth and continuous bloom, and a mid-season trim can rejuvenate the planting if it becomes overly leggy in the heat of summer.

common_name: Purple Wave Petunia (Original Groundcover Spreading Petunia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Purple Wave spreads low and wide rather than mounding upright, making it useful as a flowering groundcover as well as a container and hanging basket plant.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, spacing plants generously to allow for their wide spread. Introduced in the 1990s as an All-America Selections winner, Purple Wave was the original cultivar that launched the entire Wave petunia series and transformed the petunia market by introducing a genuinely low, ground-hugging, fast-spreading habit unlike the mounding upright petunias that came before it, making it useful as a colorful flowering groundcover, retaining-wall spiller, or large container filler. It blooms in vivid magenta-purple continuously from spring through frost with good heat tolerance and largely self-cleans without heavy deadheading. Regular fertilizing keeps the vigorous spreading growth flowering strongly through the season.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Campfire holds its intense orange-red color well in more sun than many coleus cultivars, though afternoon shade helps prevent scorching in peak zone 9 summer heat.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in partial shade to full sun with some afternoon shade in the hottest climates. Campfire coleus produces vividly colored foliage in glowing shades of orange and fiery red, resembling the embers of a fire and providing season-long color that rivals flowering annuals without the need for deadheading. It tolerates more direct sun than many older coleus cultivars while still performing well in bright shade, giving flexibility in siting. Pinch out flower spikes as soon as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into foliage production and to prevent it from becoming leggy, and pinch stem tips periodically to encourage bushy, well-branched growth.

common_name: Homestead Purple Verbena (Classic Groundcover Southern Verbena)

planting.note: Plant transplants after last frost in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Homestead Purple is an outstanding, extremely heat-tolerant groundcover verbena that spreads quickly and blooms almost continuously through the long Gulf South growing season.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun. Homestead Purple is one of the most celebrated groundcover verbenas ever introduced, discovered growing at an old Georgia homestead and prized for combining outstanding heat and humidity tolerance with vivid, rich purple flower clusters produced almost nonstop from spring through frost. It spreads quickly into a dense, low mat that suppresses weeds and cascades attractively over walls and the edges of raised beds, and unlike many verbena cultivars it shows good resistance to powdery mildew in humid Southern summers. It is drought-tolerant once established and needs only an occasional trim to keep it dense and encourage continued heavy bloom.

common_name: Landmark Lantana (Compact Uniform-Flowering Modern Lantana Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; the Landmark series was bred for a compact, uniform, well-branched habit and heavy, consistent flowering across a range of colors, making it popular for mass plantings and containers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun. The Landmark series was bred as a modern, more compact and uniform alternative to older, taller lantana cultivars, producing dense, well-branched mounds covered in continuous, brightly colored flower clusters across a range of available colors through the entire warm season, with strong appeal to butterflies. Its compact, predictable size makes it especially popular for mass color plantings, hanging baskets, and containers where a uniform habit is valued over the taller, more rambling growth of older cultivars like Miss Huff. It tolerates heat, humidity, and drought with ease once established and needs only light shaping to maintain a tidy mound.
